subject: HealthSync security checklist & DPA — evidence pack and dataflow deliverables
messages:
From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@healthsync.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@healthsync.com, security@healthsync.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security checklist & DPA: onboarding evidence request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick onboarding. We're finalizing our procurement checklist and need a few items before legal can clear the DPA:

- Current subprocessor roster with country of processing
- A data flow diagram showing PII ingress, processing, telemetry collection points and egress paths
- Statement on KMS/key custody (do you hold keys, use customer-managed keys, HSM details?)
- SOC 2 report or summary and any relevant attestations

Can you confirm whether any subprocessors or inference telemetry are outside the US (we have an onshore preference for this integration)? Also, roughly how long to provide the dataflow PDF and roster?

We have a HealthSync SSQ template — happy to receive the answers inline or as attachments.

Best,
Alice
Alice Wong
Security Lead, HealthSync
alice.wong@healthsync.com

---
Attachment: healthsync_ssq_template.xlsx (template)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@healthsync.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security checklist & DPA: onboarding evidence request

Hi Alice — thanks for the list and the template. We're happy to provide everything and want to make this as straightforward as possible. Quick notes and a tentative delivery plan: 

1) Subprocessor roster: attaching CSV (redwood_subprocessor_roster_20270414.csv). The roster includes processing country, purpose, and whether the subprocessors handle keyed material or telemetry.
2) Dataflow diagram: attached preliminary_dataflow_v1.pdf — this is a first-pass diagram mapping PII fields through our ingestion, tokenize/proxy layer, inference runtime, telemetry collector, and long-term logs. It intentionally omits internal hostnames.
3) KMS/key custody: summary attached (redwood_soc2_summary_2027.txt) — we operate customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and use our managed KMS for hosted customers; we can provide an attestation statement for the hosted flow or support a key-split/HSM integration for your team if preferred.
4) SOC 2: we can provide our SOC 2 Type II summary report and a pointer to the auditor's letter under NDA.

Questions for you so we can tailor the artifacts:
- Is HealthSync requiring an explicit onshore-only covenant for subprocessors, or is an approval flow acceptable (i.e., notify + allow HealthSync to deny offshore subprocessors)?
- Do you need field-level PII classification mapping (CSV) or is the diagram + high-level list sufficient for initial legal review?

Estimated timeline: roster + PDF + SOC2 summary by EOD Apr 14. If you need additional artifacts (KMS attestation letter, redlines), allow 48 hours.

Deliverables attached: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20270414.csv; preliminary_dataflow_v1.pdf; redwood_soc2_summary_2027.txt

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

---
Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20270414.csv; preliminary_dataflow_v1.pdf; redwood_soc2_summary_2027.txt

From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@healthsync.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@healthsync.com, security@healthsync.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security checklist & DPA: onboarding evidence request

Thanks Soojin — received the attachments and quick review notes below. A few clarifications that legal needs before we can proceed: 

- For the subprocessor roster, can you add a simple column that states whether the subprocessors have access to de-identified telemetry versus raw PII? That's the item our privacy counsel flags most.
- Onshore preference: HealthSync's default is onshore-only for any provider that processes medical PII, but we can make exceptions if you commit to:
  a) country-by-country roster updates prior to onboarding a new subprocessor, and
  b) a contractual limit to specific allowed countries (OECD list or explicit list).
- KMS attestation: we need a short statement confirming whether Redwood holds full key custody for any production PII payloads for hosted customers. If yes, please describe HSM vendor and key rotation cadence.

I'll attach our SSQ filled with the high-level answers for you to review. If you can update the roster CSV and confirm the KMS wording, we can escalate to Legal for a DPA redline pass.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alice

---
Attachment: healthsync_ssq_filled_v1.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: HealthSync security checklist & DPA: onboarding evidence request

Looping in legal/procurement to prepare the DPA and propose a standstill on offshore subprocessors until HealthSync signs. Marissa — can you take point on DPA redlines? Suggested starting items:

- Add a subprocessor approval clause: Redwood will provide 10 business days' notice and allow Customer to object; if Customer objects, Redwood will either not engage or provide reasonable mitigation.
- Consider limiting allowed processing countries to OECD + explicitly listed exceptions; we should avoid a blanket onshore-only commit without commercial offset.
- Prepare a short KMS attestation (1 paragraph) describing hosted vs private key custody and include HSM vendor (e.g., AWS KMS / HSM).

Soojin — please confirm the action owner for updating the CSV with "access to raw PII vs de-identified telemetry" column. I can draft the DPA and share a DocuSign link (placeholder below).

DocuSign (draft): https://app.docusign.com/redwood/dpa/HS-3741 

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Platform Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@healthsync.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, procurement@healthsync.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security checklist & DPA: onboarding evidence request

Alice / HealthSync team — thanks for the clarifications. Attached is an updated roster with the requested column (redwood_subprocessor_roster_20270414_updated.csv) and an annotated dataflow diagram that highlights PII fields and telemetry collection points. Key points: 

- Subprocessors: the updated CSV flags subprocessors that only receive de-identified telemetry. We have two infra subprocessors located in EU/APAC that handle ephemeral telemetry for routing and autoscaling; they do not receive raw PII.
- KMS: For the hosted API, Redwood operates a managed KMS (AWS KMS backed HSM) and holds operational custody of keys; we rotate keys every 90 days and can provide a short attestation letter for hosted customers. For Private deployments, we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) and HSM integrations — customers retain custody.
- SOC 2: link to summary included; full report can be shared under a mutual NDA.

Next steps we propose:
1) I'll upload the updated artifacts to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/healthsync/dataflow_v1 (contains CSV + annotated PDF + SOC2 summary).
2) Marissa will follow up with a DPA redline via DocuSign.
3) If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the diagram and answer any privacy counsel questions.

Deliverables attached: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20270414_updated.csv; preliminary_dataflow_v1_annotated.pdf; redwood_kms_attestation_hosted_20270414.txt; redwood_dpa_draft_20270414.docx

Please confirm which time window works for the call and whether the DOCS we provided are sufficient for legal to start redlines.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0132
